items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1962-09-19
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Now, I read somewhere, Mr. Armstrong, that Jack Teagarden once described you as just a little guy with a big mouth... [INTERVIEWEE] That's right.

ctx.x: Satchmo, isn't it? Satchmo, yeah. That's the nickname I picked up in England, you know. In England? Yeah, when I went there in 1932, I met the editor of the Melody Maker, who was Percy Brooks at the time. And at that time, my nickname was Satchel Mouth. See, like the valise, you know what I mean? And now, I don't know, when the train pulled up and Percy Brooks come up, he said, hello, Satchmo, you know. So I said, what'd you say, Daddy? You know, that's what we agreed with. And then I asked my trombone player,…
Now, I read somewhere, Mr. Armstrong, that Jack Teagarden once described you as just a little guy with a big mouth, but man, can he blow that horn?

items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-02
items.q: We never did worry about when we go to a studio together... I dropped my bags 1.30 that morning and went right down to the round table where Jack was playing and got up on the stand and finished the last hour.

ctx.x: You were talking earlier about the orchestras in the old days and the playing for the funerals and the impromptu stuff on the street corner. Is that being done at all anymore? Who's doing it? Are these names? The younger generation. Are we going to hear from them?

Well, it'll be some down there. But I think they got the wrong idea about things. They want to blow the roof off. All volume and no feeling. Yeah. And then we look around, the chop's tied. Yeah. But in my days coming up, like a man like old man Morett, he was way up in age. See, and there were several trumpet players that instilled things in me and I admired and I never forgot. And most of my education is observing. See, now, there's old man Morett, he had a brass band, oh, about 15, 20 pieces. And every time he…
You do it any time. Of the fellows that started out with you, are any of them still around playing?
